recentItems.title: Nepalese army assists as authorities continue to find flood survivors and transport them to safety
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Trishuli, Nuwakot District, Nepal - 29 August 2026
1. Various of excavators moving through mud-filled road in damaged area
2. Various of Shoba Shretha feeding her dog, ‘Sweetie,’ who they found today

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot District, Nepal – 29 August 2026
3. Wide of relatives of missing people holding up photos with their names
4. Close of poster with photo of Milan Kharel, who was working at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa
5. SOUNDBITE (English) Priti Kharel, sister of Milan Kharel:
"It’s already four days. I don’t know, my brother, he might be trapped inside the tunnel area of the upper Trishuli hydropower 206 MW 1. So, we are trying to know his actual information, I don’t know in which state he is now. Either alive or dead or which situation. So, as per his friends, those (who) were rescued, his friends, so we came to know that he also can be inside the tunnel, he also can be trapped inside the tunnel. So, we want government to rescue as soon as possible.”
6. Wide of rescued people being taken for medical check-up at army camp
7. Soldiers arriving in trucks
8. Various of relatives of missing people waiting outside army camp for news of their loved ones
9. Wide of army personnel posting list of names of rescued people
10. Ambulance inside army camp
11. Wide of Puran Tamang, who was rescued two days ago near a tunnel in Mailung, inside army camp
12. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Puran Tamang, rescued man:
“I had no hope of surviving, inside there (the tunnel). I had a narrow escape.”
13. Close of injury on his forehead
14. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Puran Tamang, rescued man:
 “I have nothing left with me now except for two, three clothes. All my documents were washed away, I have nothing.”
15. Wide of Buddhi Tamang, who was rescued two days ago, sitting inside army camp
16. Close of Tamang eating biscuit
17. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Buddhi Tamang, rescued man:
“I don't know how I managed to survive from inside there (the tunnel). While we were getting out from there, lots of people were dead inside the tunnel.”
18. Wide of army personnel unloading aid from truck
19. Wide of relief material kept on ground
20. Various of army personnel picking up relief material
STORYLINE:
Nepalese army personnel assisted in continued efforts on Saturday to find survivors of the catastrophic flash flood and transport them to safety. 

At relief centers, as some arrived, families waited anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

After Nepali authorities updated their figures Saturday, the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 633 dead and nearly 3,000 people missing. Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing.

As people were still evacuating from Trishuli, some village residents were returning to see what could be salvaged from their decimated homes.

Shoba Shretha, returned to find her dog, Sweetie, who she was forced to leave behind when the floods came. Shretha sat on the ground petting her and feeding her water from a bottle. 

At some point, relief coordinators cleared villagers, press and volunteers from the entrance to Trishuli, as excavation equipment drove into the flooded village, continuing to dig.

Search and rescue efforts continued at several locations in Nepal and China’s Tibet, including the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the severely damaged Gyirong border crossing on the Chinese side.







AP Video by: Shonal Ganguly, Victoria Milko, Dar Yasin

recentItems.title: Nepali authorities continue relief efforts and rescues in areas impacted by the flash floods
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot District, Nepal - 29 August 2026
1. Various of people rescued from flood-hit areas being helped out of a military helicopter and taken to a makeshift medical center
2. Elderly woman being carried by a Nepalese army soldier
3. Various of rescued people disembarking helicopter
4. Child being carried by a Nepalese army soldier
5. Rescued man being helped by Nepalese army personnel
6. Nepalese army personnel holding child
7. Various of rescued mother holding her child
8. Wide of Nepalese army doctors and medical team examining woman
9. Various of army doctor removing an old bandage from rescued man's feet
10. Wide of people checking a list of rescued people for the names of missing loved ones
11. Various of Rajesh Kumar Ram checking the list for his son's name
12. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Rajesh Kumar Ram, looking for his son:
“I’m hopeful, by chance that my son is somewhere. Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I’m waiting for that moment only.”
13. Various of Nepalese army personnel preparing to head to flood-affected areas for rescue operations
14. Various of Nepalese army personnel loading relief supplies onto helicopter
15. Helicopter taking off
STORYLINE:
Poor weather temporarily hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal on Saturday as the search for thousands of missing people in areas devastated by catastrophic flash floods along the border with China entered its fourth day.

Rescue workers and military personnel have been working around the clock since Wednesday’s disaster, which killed more than 600 people and left about 3,000 missing. Some survivors have been pulled from the mud, while crews continue searching several locations for those still missing.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, a Nepali Army spokesperson, said helicopter operations were temporarily suspended Saturday morning because of poor weather. Flights resumed in some areas later in the day.

In Nuwakot, one of the districts badly affected by the floods, Associated Press journalists saw helicopters resume operations before noon.

Some helicopters arrived carrying survivors from flood-hit areas, while others were loaded with relief supplies including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice before heading back toward affected communities.

An older man was carefully helped from one helicopter while a soldier carried an older woman on his back to a makeshift medical center. Medics checked her blood pressure, breathing and heartbeat.

Several babies were also among those evacuated from the nearby community of Trishuli with soldiers carrying them from the helicopters to safety.

Most evacuees arrived with little more than the clothes they were wearing, and in some cases a small plastic bag.

At a relief center in Nuwakot, families waited anxiously for information about relatives still missing.

Military personnel posted sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people on a wall. Families crowded around the lists, scanning the names, taking photographs and wiping away tears.

Among those waiting was Rajesh Kumar Ram, who was looking for his son. “I’m hopeful, by chance that my son is somewhere. Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I’m waiting for that moment only,” he said.

Outside the relief center, mud-covered streets offered a stark reminder of the destruction left by the floods. A truck sat stuck in the mud, its bed raised into the air.

The rescue and relief operations are continuing as authorities search for those still missing and deliver supplies to communities cut off by the disaster.

AP video by: Shonal Ganguly

Poor weather temporarily hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal on Saturday as the search for thousands of missing people in areas devastated by catastrophic flash floods along the border with China entered its fourth day.

Rescue workers and military personnel have been working around the clock since Wednesday’s disaster, which killed more than 600 people and left about 3,000 missing.

Flights resumed in some areas later in the day.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon Saturday, Associated Press journalists saw.

Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. 

Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

An older man was carefully helped off one helicopter, while a soldier carried an older woman on his back to a medical tent. 

There, medics checked her blood pressure, breathing and heartbeat, as well as her teeth and gums.

Most of those evacuated arrived with nothing except the clothes they were wearing and, in some cases, a small plastic bag.

About a dozen people emerged from another helicopter. 

Soldiers carried several babies who had also been evacuated.

The evacuees had been brought from the nearby community of Trishuli.

recentItems.title: How international supermarkets in the US might break up a dinner rut without costing a fortune
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
1. Various of grocery store worker Bailey Hughes bagging groceries at checkout
2. Customers walking into international food market store

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York – 30 June 2026
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Beryl Shereshewsky, content creator:
“I think if you're trying to expand your eating habits at home and you want to try new things, what you could do is look at something you really like and see the iterations of it around the world. So hypothetically, if you do really like tomato and cucumber salads, you could look that up and see how other cultures are doing it and that way you add a couple of new ingredients and you're trying something new from something that's familiar.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
4. Customers looking at items in snack aisle

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York – 30 June 2026
5. SOUNDBITE (English) Beryl Shereshewsky, Food Content Creator:
“Everywhere you go in America, you're going to find immigrants and those immigrants are still cooking their foods from their countries and cultures and they need supermarkets to do that. So, I think you would be surprised by how many markets, international markets exist, even in small towns and cities.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
6. Close of produce on shelf

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York – 30 June 2026
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Beryl Shereshewsky, Food Content Creator:
“I found that the same dish could be found in different countries. And so, there is this one thing that even though we speak different languages or we wear different clothing, we live in different places, like suddenly we're all connected through a tomato.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
8. Various of Hughes serving customer at checkout 
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Bailey Hughes, cashier, Idaho Capital Asian Market:
“So, like it's exciting when people come in here for the first time because it can be overwhelming because you can see how big this store is. People will come in sometimes because they saw something viral on the internet.”
10. Customers looking at food on shelf
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Palina Louangketh, director, Idaho Museum of International Diaspora:
“You know, coming here to an international market, you get both a dose of cultural experience but also healthy, fresh, exotic ingredients that they can incorporate into their own kitchen.”
12. Customers looking at items in snack aisle

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York – 30 June 2026
13. SOUNDBITE (English) Beryl Shereshewsky, Food Content Creator:
“Produce tends to be cheaper at international markets. And if you're for something from that market's cuisine, if you are at an Asian supermarket, Asian sauces and condiments and kind of items are going to be a lot cheaper there because they're catering to that community.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
14. Hughes scanning and bagging groceries at store

ASSOCIATED PRESS
New York – 30 June 2026
15. SOUNDBITE (English) Beryl Shereshewsky, Food Content Creator:
“If you're shopping on a budget, I do think it's a good idea to try to find those niche supermarkets because you will save money versus finding the products online or going to, you know, like a big box supermarket where there is an ethnic aisle.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Boise, Idaho – 13 June 2026
16. Exterior of Idaho Capital Asian Market
17. Idaho Asian Plaza sign
STORYLINE:
When kitchen burnout hits, figuring out what to make for dinner every day can feel like an impossible task.

STORYLINE:
When kitchen burnout hits, figuring out what to make for dinner every day can feel like an impossible task. 

Eating out or relying on convenience foods are increasingly difficult solutions for many American families, who are facing the biggest jump in grocery prices in a half century.

It can also be healthier to cook at home, where it is easier to control things like how much salt or sugar is added to a meal.

But in many cities, there's another way to break the “what's for dinner” rut without breaking the bank: shopping at international food markets.

It can be surprisingly simple to incorporate new flavors into home meals by pairing unfamiliar ingredients with pantry staples, says Palina Louangketh, a self-described foodie and the director of the Idaho Museum of International Diaspora.

recentItems.title: Monthslong drought and extreme heat put a burden on fisheries across Central and Eastern Europe
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++PART MUTE++ 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Trebinje, Bosnia Herzegovina - 23 August 2026
1. Wide of fish farm staff walking 
2. Mid of staff checking the fish
3. Wide of fish farm staff feeding fish
4. Pan of fish eating in the pond
5. Mid of the fish farm owner Veljko Budjen looking at the pond
6. Mid of fish
7. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Veljko Budjen, fish farm owner: 
"In the last five years I have been seeing dramatic changes in the ecosystem and environment, which are all consequence of global warming, and that directly affects fish production, especially trout. Trout is a cold-water fish, which requires cold water with a lot of oxygen. Carp is less in danger here. But I can also say that we see changes with sea-water fish as well. Sea bass cannot be grown already in some of the farms while sea bream can be grown still. The sea temperature now is over 30 degrees Celsius, so large-scale production is difficult.” 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Petrovaradin, Serbia - 25 August 2026
8. Drone shot of the drying Dunavac, a side branch of the Danube River ++MUTE++
9. Mid of small fish in the water
10. Wide of the drying out Dunavac side branch
11. Drone shot of the side branch ++MUTE++
12. Mid of small boat on dry
13. Close of the cracked riverbed
14. Wide of small boats on dry
15. Close of a shell sitting on dry inlet bed
16. Drone shot of the dry river bed ++MUTE++
17. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Dusan Jovanovic, fisherman at the Dunavac hobby fishermen’s association: 
"This year we have extreme temperatures and none of us remembers such low water levels, not even the older generations. The water has run out, and the Dunavac inlet has receded as much as it could. Only a little water has remained. Our association has reacted to the situation, asking Vode Vojvodine (a state company managing the rivers of northern Serbia) in charge of this fishing area to do something and to save the fish here.”
18. Drone shot of the dry riverbank ++MUTE++

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Belgrade, Serbia - 6 August 2026
19. Wide of radar dome of Serbian Hydrometeorological Institute
20. Wide of Serbian and the Hydrometeorological Institute flags 
21. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Jelena Jerinic, chief hydrologist of the Serbian Hydrometeorological Institute: 
"Facts show us hydrologists that the constant weather extremes repeat year after year. This is very odd. In 2012, we had extreme ice, in 2014 there were historic floods, two years ago we had a major drought on small- and mid-sized rivers, which was the biological minimum on all rivers in Serbia. This year we have a big drought on the Danube. We’ll see what comes next.”

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Rožmberk, Czech Republic - 26 August 2026
22. Wide of fishermen in their boats
23. Wide of fisherman in the water
24. Pan of fishermen setting a net
25. SOUNDBITE (Czech) Jan Sokolik, technician at Rybarstvi Trebon fishery: 
"Hauls take place earlier this year. Well, it's been happening more and more earlier than before just like it used to be during the fishing seasons.”
26. Various of fishermen pulling a net
27. SOUNDBITE (Czech) Jan Sokolik, technician at Rybarstvi Trebon fishery: 
"Some ponds that were actually low on water have already been fished, but they were all the marginal ponds which had to be fished because of the water shortage caused by the drought. And now we're just starting to plan what to do next with the big ponds."
28. Various of fishermen pulling fish out of the water
STORYLINE:

The effects are showing from trout ponds in Bosnia, to the dried Danube River in Serbia to fish farms in the Czech Republic.

recentItems.title: Candles lit in Colombia capital in memory of earthquake victims
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTED SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Bogota, Colombia - 28 August 2026
1. Various of people hold a vigil for earthquake victim.
2. Various of President De La Espriella and First Lady attend vigil.
3. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Ana Lucía Pineda Colombia First Lady:
"My heart is with the victims, their families, and each of the people who were affected. But alongside this pain, a deep sense of gratitude also arises thanks to the solidarity of Colombians."
4. Various of crowd singing
5. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Pilar Cardenas, resident of Bogota:
"I believe that Colombia must turn its eyes to the Lord, and all that has happened is a strong call to the people of God to unite in prayer for Colombia."
6. Various  of people at vigil 
7. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Sara  Misnaza, Representative of the Islamic confession:
"They did not invite us as part of the religious expressions, but rather they have left us as the general public when our expression of faith might differ from the one they are currently promoting. So, in a way, this was infringing on our right to freedom of religion and worship."
8. Various of attendees holding candles



STORYLINE:
Hundreds of people gathered for a candlelight vigil in memory of the victims of the Aug. 10 earthquake in Colombia's capital.

The vigil took place at Plaza de Bolívar in Bogotá, on Friday, where mourners prayed for the dead.

The devastating 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia earlier this month.

More than 300 people were killed in the disaster according to figures published by the central government.

The quake wreaked havoc, collapsing buildings, buckling roads, crushing cars and leaving devastated residents to console one another amid the wreckage of their homes.

President Abelardo de la Espriella and first lady Ana Lucía Pineda were also present at the vigil.

Speaking to the crowd, Pineda said: “My heart is with the victims, their families, and each of the people who were affected. But alongside this pain, a deep sense of gratitude also arises thanks to the solidarity of Colombians.”

AP video by Samuel Sotomayor.

recentItems.title: Former Ecuadorian President Lenín Moreno sentenced to 5 years for corruption
recentItems.description:
(29 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTED SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Quito, Ecuador - 28 August 2026
1. Various of former Ecuadorian President Lenin Moreno arriving at court
2. Judges arriving in courtroom 
3. Judge Manuel Cabrera Esquivel opening the hearing
4. Various of proceedings
5. Various of Moreno at press conference
6. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Lenin Moreno, Former President of Ecuador:
"I don't know if there's a (political) witch hunt against me. Specifically against me. I don't know. I don't know. But something's off. Something's off. As Hamlet says, something's rotten here."
7. Lenin Moreno speaking
8. SOUNDBITE (Spanish) Lenin Moreno, Former President of Ecuador:
"I just hope that's not the verdict. I'm providing all the evidence. What else do you need to know? What I'm saying, miss, is that you should look in the right place. Look into those people who were in the habit of asking for kickbacks. So let's look into it."
9. Moreno leaving
10. Exterior of National Court of Justice
STORYLINE:
A court in Ecuador sentenced former President Lenín Moreno to five years in prison on Friday after finding him guilty of accepting bribes from the Chinese company Sinohydro for the construction of one of the Andean country’s most important hydroelectric power plants.

Along with Moreno—who was accused of being the principal perpetrator of bribery for influencing the awarding of the contract—his wife, Rocío González, and his daughter, Irina Moreno, were sentenced to 30 months in prison, and the court imposed various sentences on two brothers and a sister-in-law, from whom—according to the ruling—they received benefits and who helped cover up the payments.

Both Moreno and the other 19 defendants—one of whom was found not guilty—must repay three times the amount of illicit money received within 90 days and issue a public apology within one month.

Part of the ruling stated that Moreno’s actions in this case “constitute the crime of bribery as a principal offender,” as he used his position to intervene “and favor Sinohydro in the signing of the contract financing” to build one of the largest hydroelectric power plants in Ecuador.

According to the judges, the offense in question was committed while Moreno served as vice president (2010–2013) during the administration of then-President Rafael Correa, who is also a fugitive from justice and has been convicted in three corruption trials.

The Prosecutor's Office has requested a sentence of six years and six months in prison for the 73-year-old former leader, who has a physical disability that prevents him from walking; therefore, under Ecuadorian law, he is eligible for house arrest.

AP video by Cesar Olmos.
